title: Minimum Increments for Target Multiples in an Array
summary: Given the arrays nums and target, determine the minimum number of operations required such that each element in target has at least one multiple in nums.
statement: Given the arrays nums and target, determine the minimum number of operations required such that each element in target has at least one multiple in nums. In a single operation, you may increment any element of nums by 1.
constraints: nums has up to 50,000 positive integers and target has at most four positive integers.
Incrementing one nums element by one costs one operation.
Every target value must divide at least one resulting nums value; one nums value may cover several targets.
hints: One adjusted number covers a subset of targets exactly when it reaches a multiple of their least common multiple.
Precompute each subset LCM and update a bitmask DP once per nums value.
For every covered mask and gained subset, add the distance to the next multiple and relax their union.
Every assignment of target requirements to nums elements corresponds to one sequence of mask transitions, so the minimum transition cost is optimal.
editorial: Every assignment of target requirements to nums elements corresponds to one sequence of mask transitions, so the minimum transition cost is optimal.

tests.explanation: Increment three once to four, giving a multiple of the sole target.
Increment five once to six, whose divisibility by both targets covers them together.
